entries.title: Dressed as something else
entries.description: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.

entries.title: Colour chapters
entries.description: Every section is a chapter with its own flat colour, floor to ceiling. The page reads like a set of posters hung in a row, held together by one typeface and one grid. The colours are not decoration: they come from the subject (the brand's packaging, the artist's record sleeves, the product's own colour ways, the categories of the content) and each chapter's colour means that chapter. Decide the sequence like a designer orders a book: a strong opener, a quiet second, a surprise in the middle, a dark or very light closer.

entries.title: The contact sheet
entries.description: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.

entries.title: The dark room
entries.description: One dark field from top to bottom, and in it, lit things. Photographs and objects appear like exhibits in a dim gallery: each with space around it, each the brightest thing on its screen. Type is light, small and sparse. The darkness is not a theme switch; it is a room, and the page is a slow walk through it. It suits subjects sold on atmosphere and material: an evening restaurant, a metal card, a record, a house at dusk.

entries.title: The well-kept board
entries.description: The whole page is a board of tiles fitted edge to edge with narrow gaps, like a tidy desk seen from above. Each tile is one thing: the name, a statement, a photograph, a number, a link, a short list. There is no hero and no sequence of bands; the page is one continuous composition that the eye roams. It suits subjects with many small true things to show (a studio with work, writing, clients and news; a product with several distinct capabilities) and it replaces the generic bento by having real content in every tile and a strict system for sizes.

entries.title: The printed annual
entries.description: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.

entries.title: The object, large
entries.description: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.

entries.title: Loud and flat
entries.description: A page with the directness of a street poster: flat saturated colour, the heaviest type you can find, short blunt statements, and photographs cut out and stuck on. It is for subjects with a voice. Write the page as things a person would actually say out loud, and let the design say them at full volume. The craft is in the control beneath the noise: a strict grid, two or three colours, and exact alignment keep it from becoming a mess.

entries.title: The name as a monument
entries.description: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.

entries.title: One motif
entries.description: Take one shape from the subject and let it run the whole system. A drilling tool's octagonal cross-section becomes the buttons, the image masks and the loader. A two-account money app becomes two circles that recur as icon, inline dot and section colour. A café's striped awning becomes every band on the page. Look at the product, the logo, the object or the word in the headline and find the simplest geometry in it (a circle, an arc, a chamfer, a stripe, a notch, a ring). Then use only that shape, at three or four very different scales, everywhere a designer would normally reach for a generic rounded rectangle.

entries.title: The page is the object
entries.description: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.

entries.title: The pinned poster
entries.description: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.

entries.title: The place carries it
entries.description: For a place, the photograph is the argument. One full-bleed image of where you would be standing fills the first screen, and the design steps back: the name sits along the bottom edge like a film title, or small in a corner, and nothing else interrupts the view. The page that follows keeps that restraint: few words, large pictures, long pauses. The designer's work here is editing: choosing the one frame that makes someone want to be there, and then not covering it.

entries.title: The product performs
entries.description: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.

entries.title: The quiet instrument
entries.description: Radical understatement. Where every competitor shouts, this page almost whispers: a headline barely larger than body text, a narrow column, small exact demonstrations, and a great deal of untouched space. The restraint is the claim. It says the thing is simple, finished and sure of itself. This only works when it is carried through completely; one loud element breaks it. In the study, a tool for simple lists sold itself with a 27px headline and 12–14px copy and was one of the most confident pages in the set.

entries.title: The sentence is the layout
entries.description: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.

entries.title: The specimen catalogue
entries.description: Present what is on offer the way a field guide presents birds: each item alone on a flat colour, same scale, same angle, named plainly. A bakery's pastries become specimens and the specimens become the menu. A furniture maker's chairs each get their own colour tile. The format flatters ordinary objects because it treats each as worth looking at, and it replaces both the feature grid and the product-card grid with something that has a point of view.

entries.title: The split stage
entries.description: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.

entries.title: Type and nothing else
entries.description: The first screen is made only of words, colour and space, good enough that nobody misses a picture there. Pictures arrive later, large and few, as relief from the type. This is the honest answer when a subject has nothing worth photographing: instead of inventing illustrations, set what you have to say as well as it can be set. The typography carries a point of view through scale (one enormous statement, everything else small), through measure (a narrow, bookish column or a full-width line), and through one committed colour.

entries.title: Photographs at uneven sizes
entries.description: A calm page where the pictures are placed like prints on a gallery wall: each at its own size and position, with text set small and light between them. Nothing lines up in the obvious way, yet everything sits on a grid you can feel. The unevenness is what makes it read as art-directed by a person: a small portrait far left, a wide landscape running off the right edge, a square that overlaps the next section. It lets photographs lead without ever becoming a slideshow.

entries.title: Window that opens to the edges
uses: A flat paper or pale ground, and one picture seen through a small window that becomes the whole screen as the page scrolls. The hero is a wrapper 200svh tall holding a stage with `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh`. On the first frame the window is a 4:5 portrait opening 36% of the viewport wide (518×648px), centred, its top and bottom 126px from the edges, square corners; give it a shape from the subject if it has one (an arch, a rounded diamond, a lens). Build it as `clip-path: inset(126px 461px)` on a layer that is itself 100vw by 100svh, so the photograph or muted film inside is laid out full-bleed and never moves: only the opening grows. The headline sits left of the window on columns 1–3: two lines at clamp(44px, 4.4vw, 64px), leading 0.95, flush to the 32px margin, its last baseline level with the window's lower edge. Right of the window on columns 10–12, bottom-aligned to the same line: one supporting sentence at 18px, max 26ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Wordmark top-left and three text links top-right at 15px on the same margin; nothing else sits on the ground. Over the first 100svh of scroll the inset runs to zero on a scroll-linked timeline while the text, which sits above the picture layer, rises and fades out before the opening reaches it; the picture then holds full-bleed for 50svh before the next section slides over it. Without scroll timelines, or under reduced motion, show the open picture with the headline over a neutral scrim in its bottom-left corner.

entries.title: Team on colour tiles

Every tile is a 4:5 photograph treated identically so mixed-quality headshots look like one set: `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.15)` with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` over a flat tint, the tints rotating through four palette colours in a fixed order. Square corners or one small radius. Under each tile, left-aligned to its edge with 10px of space: the name at 15px in full ink and the role at 13px in the soft ink, up to two lines. Rows are 36px apart. A leftover tile in the last row stays at the left; it is not centred. No hover lift and no social icons.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Address in display rows
entries.description: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.

entries.title: Clip-out coupon form
entries.description: The form is a coupon to cut out. One filled card in a strong flat colour, about 2.2:1, spans columns 2–11 with a 14px radius, with 120px of ground above and below. Semicircular notches 28px across are cut into its top and bottom edges at the 46% mark with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`, and a vertical row of round dots (a dotted `border-left` 5px thick in the ground colour) joins the two notches as the perforation. Left of the perforation, with 48px padding: a two-line heading of three to five words at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px) in heavy capitals at the top, and one sentence at 16px at the bottom. Right of it: four inputs stacked with 10px gaps, each a filled block 52px tall in a lighter tone of the card with its placeholder at 16px, then a full-width solid submit bar 56px tall in the darkest ink. Inputs keep visually hidden `label` elements.

entries.title: The email as display type
entries.description: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Photo strip, three-cell bar
entries.description: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.

entries.title: Sentence, portrait, two links
entries.description: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.

entries.title: One field, nothing else
entries.description: The whole section is one prompt and one field in a column 520px wide, on the page's text column line or centred, with 200px of empty ground above and 160px below. The prompt is two lines at one size, 24–28px in medium weight: the first line in the soft ink, the second in full ink. 28px below, a single input 520px wide and 64px tall with a 12px radius, filled with the lightest tone on the page so it is the only bright surface in view; no outline at rest and a 2px inner ring in the accent on focus. Inside the right end of the field, 8px from its edge, a round submit button 44px across with an arrow and an accessible name. 16px below the field, one line at 13px says what happens next. 72px lower, three label and value rows at 14px: email, phone, address.

entries.title: Visit card on a photograph
entries.description: A full-bleed photograph of the place, 100vw by 100svh, carries one solid card and nothing else. The card is a filled panel in the paper colour, fully opaque, 380px wide with 8px corners and 32px padding, placed in the upper-right corner 60px from the top and right edges (or the upper-left: pick the corner where the photograph is calmest). It holds, top to bottom: a two- or three-word title at 28px in a light weight; the address on two lines at 16px; the opening hours as three rows with days at the left and times right-aligned in tabular figures; the phone number; then, flush with the card's bottom edge and spanning its width, a solid booking button 52px tall. The card may be `position: sticky; top: 60px` inside a taller section so it holds while the photograph scrolls beneath it. The photograph's focal point must stay clear of the card. No heading outside the card.

entries.title: The action tile
entries.description: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.

entries.title: A sentence with a blank
entries.description: The closing sentence has a gap in it, and the gap is the form. A sentence of five to eight words is set at about 6vw on two lines, flush left across columns 1–11; there is no separate heading. Where the reader's email (or name, or city) belongs, an `<input>` sits inline on the baseline: a filled block of the one-step tone, exactly one line-height tall and about 7em wide, with the placeholder in the same face and size in the softer ink, no border, and the page's radius or motif corner. The sentence's last word is the submit `<button>`, set in the same type on a block of the accent colour of the same height. Field and button use `em` units so they scale with the sentence. One line at 16px under the sentence, in the softer ink, says what happens after sending. Nothing else is in the section.

entries.title: First step, already open
entries.description: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: One word is the button
entries.description: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: The idea again, inverted
entries.description: The close flips the page's colours: ink becomes the ground and the ground becomes the ink, across a full-bleed field at least 90svh tall. The page's opening idea returns as a headline of three to five words at 9–11vw on two lines, leading 0.9, flush left, positioned in the upper two-thirds; it should echo the hero's wording, not repeat it. Along the bottom, on one shared baseline 40px above the edge: one supporting sentence at 20px in columns 1–5 and one rectangular button in the accent colour, right-aligned in columns 10–12, about 56px tall. Nothing else: no image, no second button, no logo. The field's top edge is a hard horizontal line where it meets the section above. If the footer follows on the same inverted field, leave 160px before it so the close still reads as its own screen.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: The object returns
entries.description: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page. On one flat field 90svh tall, the object's photograph occupies columns 1–8, scaled to about 130% of that area and anchored so the section's bottom and left edges crop it (`overflow: hidden` on the section; on light fields `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes a white studio background). The text sits small in columns 10–12, vertically centred: a closing line of three to five words at 32–40px, one sentence at 17px, the price or key fact on its own line at 22px, and one rectangular button. Nothing overlaps the object's focal area. Where the page's subject is a shape rather than a photograph, the page's motif takes the object's place at the same scale as a flat filled shape. The closing line is the only heading.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Three photographs, then a field
entries.description: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Last photograph, text beside
entries.description: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm. All text is confined to the right half and never crosses the centre line: in columns 8–12, anchored to the lower third, a closing line of three to five words at about 3.4vw in a light weight, a paragraph of two or three lines at 17px, and one filled button in the paper colour with ink text, about 52px tall. If the image behind the text is not calm enough, darken the whole photograph slightly with `filter: brightness(0.8)` rather than laying a panel behind the words. The section butts directly against a footer in one solid colour, so the photograph's bottom edge is a hard line. No logo, no second action.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: A plain sentence, one action
entries.description: The page ends on an almost empty screen. On the page ground, with no band and no panel, one sentence of eight to fourteen words is set at 18–22px in the regular weight, in the full ink, no wider than 34ch, on the same left edge as the page's text column (or centred only if the whole page is centred). 24px beneath it sits one small filled button, about 40px tall with 18px side padding, and optionally one text link beside it on the same baseline. That is all. Above the sentence leave at least 30svh of empty ground and below it at least 20svh before the footer line, so the emptiness reads as decided. The sentence is written as something a person would say, and it names the action plainly. No headline-sized type appears anywhere in this section.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Question at both edges
entries.description: For a closing choice between two answers: book or ask, this date or that, the tasting or the tour. A flat field exactly 100svh tall in the darkest tone. The question is a two-line heading at clamp(110px, 11vw, 168px), leading 1.0, centred, about 54% of the width: line one with its cap line 32px under the field's top edge, line two with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The band of about 560px between them is empty except for one row at its optical centre: two solid rectangular buttons, each about 200×56px with its label at 18px in medium weight, their inner edges 120px either side of the centre axis, and between them, exactly on the axis, the word 'or' at 18px in the soft ink. 16px under the row, centred, one line at 16px in the soft ink says what happens after either choice. The type above and below closes the empty band, so it reads as held breath rather than a gap.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: The reply card
entries.description: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Questions beside a tall photograph
entries.description: One field in a deep or pale flat tone, split 5 to 7. Left, columns 1–5: a heading of two to four words at 36–44px; under it the three or four practical facts people ask first (address, times, how to arrive) as plain lines at 18px; then five or six questions as an accordion with no lines between rows, only 28px of space. Each question is a `<summary>` at 20px with a small chevron drawn from two 2px strokes at its right; the open answer sits beneath at 17px in the softer ink, on the same left edge. One filled button and one text link close the column. Right, columns 7–12: a tall photograph (3:4) that bleeds off the top edge of the section and stops 80px short of the bottom, with a second, square photograph a third of its width overlapping its lower-left corner by 40px.

entries.title: A band per question
entries.description: Each question owns a full-bleed band, and the bands alternate between two flat tones (ground and one step away, or two palette colours with their assigned inks) and butt together with no gap. Inside every band the same grid applies: the question in columns 1–5 at 28–32px bold, top-aligned with 56px of padding above; the answer in columns 7–12 at 18px with leading 1.5, the same padding, and 56px below. Bands are as tall as their content, so their heights differ, which gives the stack its rhythm. Four to seven bands. The heading is the first band: two to four words at about 7vw on the accent colour, flush left, taller than the rest at about 40svh with the words anchored to its bottom-left. All answers are visible; there are no toggles.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Accordion of filled tiles
entries.description: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Large questions, answers beside
entries.description: Every answer is open; nothing collapses. Each question-and-answer pair is a row on the 12-column grid: the question in columns 1–6 at clamp(26px, 2.6vw, 40px), medium weight, leading 1.1, no more than two lines; its answer in columns 8–12 at 17–18px with leading 1.55 and a measure near 40ch, its first baseline level with the question's first baseline. Rows are separated by 72–88px of empty space and nothing else. Five to seven rows. The section heading, two or three words, is set at the same size as the questions but in the softer ink and sits as the first row's left cell with an empty right cell, so it reads as the top of the same table rather than a title above it. Because questions are large and answers small, the left column works as a scannable index.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Answers as reading text
entries.description: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Question index, one answer
entries.description: Questions on the left, one answer on the right, and the answer changes as the reader moves through the questions. Columns 1–5 list all questions at one size, 18px, with 18px between them; each is preceded by a solid dot 8px across, in the softer ink when idle and in the accent colour when selected. The selected question is in the full ink, the rest in the softer ink. Columns 7–12 hold the answer pane, `position: sticky; top: 120px`: the selected answer at 24–28px in the regular weight, leading 1.3, measure about 30ch, so the answer, not the question, is the large type. Selection follows hover, click and keyboard focus; the pane crossfades in 150ms. The first question is selected on load. A two-word heading in the softer ink is the first line of the list, at the same 18px.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Tabbed index cards
entries.description: Questions are filed like cards in a drawer. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw sits in columns 3–10. Beneath it, in the same columns, five or six filled panels are stacked so that each overlaps the one above, leaving 96px of every card showing. Each card has a tab on its top edge, 200px wide and 40px tall, stepping right by 150px per card, cut with `clip-path: polygon()` so card and tab are one filled shape. The cards rotate through two or three palette colours. The tab carries the topic in one or two words at 16px; the visible strip under it shows the question at 20px medium. Choosing a card expands it to show the answer at 17px over at most 50ch and pushes the cards below it down. One card is open at a time; the first is open on load.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Wide heading, indented questions
entries.description: A heading of three to five words at about 5.5vw runs from the left margin on one or two lines and is the only large thing in the section. 80px beneath it the questions begin, indented to start at column 5 and running to column 12, so the left third under the heading stays empty. Each question is a row at 22–24px in the regular weight with a chevron of two 2px strokes at the far right; rows are separated by 36px of space and no rules. Opening a row lays a tile of the one-step tone behind that row and its answer (24px padding, extending 24px beyond the text on both sides) and shows the answer at 17px with a 48ch measure. Six questions. Nothing else shares the screen; the indent against the wide heading is the composition. Build with `<details>`.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Capabilities as a menu
entries.description: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list. One paper-coloured sheet, 520–600px wide and taller than it is wide, sits on a contrasting flat ground, centred or starting at column 2; its top and bottom edges are cut into shallow scallops or a zigzag with clip-path, its sides straight. On it, centred at the top, the heading: two or three words at 44–56px, then 40px of space. Below, items in two or three groups; each group opens with its name at 20px bold. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, a short value on the right (a price, a time, a quantity, 'included'), and between them a leader of round 4px dots (border-bottom: 4px dotted, sitting on the baseline). A description at 15px in the soft ink sits under the name, at most 34ch. 18px between items, 44px between groups.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Capabilities at poster scale
entries.description: No images. The heading, two to four words, is the first line of the list itself, set at the same size as the items but in the soft ink, so no separate title sits above. Five to eight capability names follow, one per line, at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 84px), medium to heavy weight, leading 1.0, tight tracking, flush left on the page margin across columns 1–8 of 12. Each name's one-sentence description is set at 16–18px in columns 9–12, its first baseline aligned with the name's baseline (CSS grid, align-items: first baseline). Rows are separated by 0.35em of space and nothing else. On hover one row keeps full ink while the others fall to 35% opacity. Leave 18–22vh of empty ground above and below; nothing else shares the section.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Close-ups on a board
entries.description: A board of filled tiles, each a macro view of one small part of the interface. A 12-column grid with 8px gaps, 104px rows and 10px outer margins, no empty cells, no outlines. Eight tiles in four sizes: 6×4, 6×2, 3×4 and 3×2 (columns × rows). Each tile is a flat palette colour with overflow: hidden and holds one real element, built in em and enlarged to 300–400% through the font-size of its data-ui root: a toggle, a pair of key caps, a status word on its block, one figure from a readout, a slider thumb on its track, three stacked initials discs. The element is pushed off-centre so two of the tile's edges crop it. Bottom-left in every tile, 20px in: the capability's name at 18px medium and one line at 15px. One 6×2 tile holds only the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), top-left.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Comparison set as text
entries.description: A comparison table with no lines and no tick marks. A CSS grid: capability names in columns 1–5 of 12 at 22–24px medium, then three answer columns of equal width (plans, methods, or this against the usual way). Every cell answers in words at 17px: 'Yes, unlimited', 'Up to five', 'Not yet', never a symbol. Seven to ten rows, each 64–72px tall, with every other row on a ground one tone darker so the eye tracks across; rows touch. The column that matters is one filled block in the accent or ink colour running the full height of the table behind its cells and rising 24px above the first row, with its text reversed. Column names sit in the top row at 17px bold. The heading, two to four words at 40–48px, hangs top-left above column 1 with 48px beneath.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Fixed output, live controls
entries.description: A split the reader operates. Left, columns 1–6: a flat colour field that is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh, edge to edge, holding one thing the product makes (a card, an email, a chart, a rendered page) centred at true size, about 420px wide, root marked data-ui. Right, columns 8–12: a reading column no wider than 44ch, with four or five capability blocks 50vh apart. Each block is a sentence at 28–32px, a paragraph at 17px, and directly beneath it one real control at interface size: a slider, a segmented choice, a toggle, a short text field. Operating a control changes the fixed output on the left at once, and changes persist, so by the last block the reader has configured their own. The section heading, two to four words at 40–44px, opens the right column, 72px from the top.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Four cards dealt into a fan
entries.description: Four values, rules or features, each on a card dealt onto the table as the page scrolls. A wrapper about 400svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh on the page's darkest flat ground. Each card is a portrait panel of 340×400px with a 20px radius, filled with its own palette colour (four colours that differ clearly in lightness), no border, no shadow. On a card, with 28px padding: its name at 32px in heavy capitals on one or two lines at the top, a photograph or a single picture of the thing at 60% of the card's width in the middle, and one sentence at 16px at the foot. Card one lands alone at the centre; each further quarter of the wrapper deals the next from below the bottom edge, landing 250px to the right of the one before, rotated between -4 and 4 degrees and overlapping only its right 90px, until the four form a fan about 1,090px wide centred on the stage. Keep each card's name, picture and sentence inside its left 240px, so no card ever covers another's words. In the study the cards overlap by two thirds and bury the earlier titles; here nothing lies on top of text. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4vw, 60px), sits top-left on the stage on the 32px margin with one sentence at 17px under it. The stage releases after the fourth card has settled; under reduced motion the fan is simply there.

entries.title: Giant command list
entries.description: The capabilities are set as the product's own command menu, scaled up until it is the section; the root is marked data-ui. First a real search `<input>` at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px) across columns 1–10: a filled block one tone off the ground, 1.9em tall, whose placeholder of two to four words serves as the heading ('Find a command'). Beneath it six to eight capability names, one per line, at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 76px), leading 1.1, flush left, each row the full content width. At the right end of a row sits its shortcut as key caps: filled squares 1em tall, one character each, in the text face. The selected row lies on a solid block of the accent colour and shows one sentence at 17px under its name. Typing filters the rows; arrow keys and hover move the selection. Nothing else is in the section.

entries.title: Mosaic of unlike tiles
entries.description: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and rows of 96px, filled with no empty cells and no outlines. Six to eight filled tiles in four sizes only: 6×5, 6×3, 3×3 and 3×2 (columns × rows). The rule that keeps it from being a card grid: no two neighbouring tiles hold the same kind of thing. One tile is the heading alone, two to four words at 4vw, top-left. One is a photograph covering its tile. One is a single figure at 6vw with a caption. One is a short list of four lines at 20px. The others are a single sentence each at 28–32px. Text sits top-left with 24px padding; tiles holding one sentence leave their lower half empty. Tile fills: the ground one tone darker, two palette colours, and photographs. One corner radius everywhere, either 0 or 8px.

entries.title: One scene, stepping statements
entries.description: A wrapper 350–450vh tall holds a sticky full-bleed photograph (100vw by 100svh) with a calm, symmetrical subject and a clear upper third; a neutral dark scrim covers only that upper third. At top centre, five or six short statements of two to five words are stacked at 18–20px with 10px between them; the first of them is the section's heading. One statement is at full white and the rest at 45% opacity; the active line steps down the stack as the reader scrolls (IntersectionObserver on invisible 70vh markers). For each statement, two small photographs with square corners, 160–240px wide and of different ratios, fade in left and right of the centre line at different heights, then leave when the next pair arrives. No other text. A low-key image on a deep ground works equally well.

entries.title: One-size name columns
entries.description: Pure text at one size. Three columns start on columns 1, 4 and 7 of the 12-column grid, leaving columns 10–12 empty on purpose. Each column opens with a group name in full ink and continues with a tight stack of six to ten capability names in the soft ink, all at 16–17px, regular weight, line-height 1.25, no bullets and no symbols; one blank line separates group name from stack. Hovering a name brings it to full ink and shows a one-line description in a fixed spot: the top of the empty columns 10–12, at the same size. The heading is no larger than 28px; two or three words, alone on column 1, 96px above the columns. Give the section 20vh of empty ground above and below, so the smallness reads as decided. Works on light or deep grounds.

entries.title: Panel with margin notes
entries.description: One tall panel from the product is shown whole, like a plate in a manual, with notes in both margins. The panel (an inspector, a sidebar, a composer) is built at true size, 360–400px wide and 640–720px tall, root marked data-ui, and stands in columns 5–8 on the plain ground with no stage behind it. Six notes describe six of its parts: three in columns 1–4, right-aligned, and three in columns 9–12, left-aligned, each 24ch wide and placed by absolute top offsets so its first line is level with the control it explains. A note is a name at 18px medium and two lines at 15px in the soft ink. Hovering or focusing a note keeps its control at full strength and drops the rest of the panel to 30% opacity; the controls themselves also work. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits right-aligned in columns 1–4, level with the panel's top edge.

entries.title: Paragraph with picture words
entries.description: One paragraph does the work of a feature grid. Three or four sentences, 35–50 words in total, set at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px), leading 1.18, medium weight, across columns 1–11, left-aligned. Each sentence names one capability, and directly after that capability's key noun sits an inline slot: an inline-block frame 1em tall and 1.9em wide, radius 0.18em, dropped 0.12em below the baseline, holding a tight photograph crop (object-fit: cover) or a real interface control at readable size. Four slots at most, never two on one line. The nouns keep the weight and colour of the rest; the slots are the only emphasis. Mark it up as a paragraph and give the section a visually hidden heading of two or three words; nothing visible sits above. 72px lower, starting at column 7, one supporting sentence at 18px and the action.

entries.title: Pinned heading, passing rows
entries.description: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content. Columns 1–5: the heading, two or three words, at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px) in the heaviest weight, position: sticky; top: 32px, so it holds while the right side travels. Columns 7–12: four to six capability blocks stacked with 120px between them. Each block is a title at 28px bold, then a two-part row: a portrait photograph at 3:4, 180–220px wide with square corners, and beside it, top-aligned, a plain list of four to six short lines at 18px with 14px between lines. Photographs alternate between the left and the right of their list, so the column does not read as a ladder. One ink colour, chosen for contrast on the field. The heading releases when the bottom of the last block reaches it.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Rows with margin photographs
entries.description: Everything hangs from one vertical axis at column 5, about 35% of the width. First the heading: a statement of up to five words at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px) starting on the axis, vertically centred in an otherwise empty 70svh of ground. Then four or five benefit rows, each starting on the same axis: a title at clamp(28px, 3vw, 48px) and under it a paragraph of 34ch at 17px. Columns 1–4 stay empty. At the right margin each row carries one photograph, top-aligned with its title and deliberately unequal: 240px wide at 4:5 in one row, 320px at 3:2 in the next, 180px square after that. Rows are separated by 96–120px of space, not lines. On a saturated field, set all type in one pale ink and leave the photographs ungraded.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Sentences with switches
entries.description: Four or five capabilities, each one plain sentence of five to eight words about what the product will do for you, each ending in a working switch. Every sentence is a full-bleed band 20vh tall, butted against the next with no gap. Inside, on the 12-column grid: the sentence at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px) on one line in columns 1–10, vertically centred; in columns 11–12, right-aligned, the product's real toggle, built in em with its root marked data-ui, 1.1em tall so it matches the type. Off, a band is the page ground and its sentence is in the soft ink. On, the band fills with a palette colour, a different one per band, the sentence turns to full ink and a second line at 17px appears beneath stating the consequence in figures. Two bands are on at load. Toggles answer click, Space and Enter. There is no heading; the first sentence does that work.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Shape-marked small points
entries.description: For the many minor points that do not deserve a row each. Columns 1–5: one photograph inside a single large shape taken from the subject's own geometry (a circle, an arch, a chamfered block), made with clip-path or border-radius, about 78svh tall and pushed 12% past the section's left edge so the viewport crops it. Columns 7–12: the heading, two to four words at 40–48px, then 56px lower a grid of eight to twelve points in three columns with 40px column gaps and 44px row gaps, no cells and no fills. Each point is a title at 17px medium preceded by the same shape drawn at cap height (0.7em, flat fill, inline SVG or a styled span), then two lines at 15px in the soft ink. The small shapes take a different palette colour per column, which is the only colour on the right side.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Small proof beside text
entries.description: One narrow module repeated four to six times down the page, never alternating sides. Each module is 640px wide at most and starts on the page's text margin (at about 22% of the viewport on an understated page). Left part: a flat panel 360px wide and 120 to 200px tall, one tone off the ground, radius 8px, holding one small exact demonstration: a cropped interface fragment at true size, or a tightly cropped photograph covering the panel. Right part, 20px away and top-aligned: a heading of one or two lines at 18px medium and two short paragraphs at 15px in the soft ink, in a column 250px wide. Panel heights vary with their content; text always hangs from the panel's top edge. 96–120px of empty ground between modules. The section heading is 24–28px, on the same left edge, 64px above the first module. In a column under 600px the text moves beneath its panel.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Specimens on colour tiles
entries.description: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Stacking colour sheets
entries.description: Three to five capabilities, each a full-width flat colour sheet about 86svh tall with only its top corners rounded at 28px. Every sheet is position: sticky, with top offsets rising by 72px from one sheet to the next, so each new sheet slides up over the last and leaves the previous sheet's title band showing, like tabbed folders in a drawer. Inside a sheet: the capability name top-left at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), sitting within that 72px band; a paragraph of up to 40ch at 18px bottom-left; and in columns 7–12 one photograph filling the sheet from below the band to the bottom edge, square corners, no inset. Sheet colours follow the palette in a fixed order, with ink chosen per sheet. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px), sits on the ground above the stack with 48px beneath and scrolls away normally.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Staggered fragment cells
entries.description: A three-column grid of six filled cells with 8px gaps, each cell 420–460px tall and filled one tone off the ground, no outlines. Every cell has two parts: a text part (a title at 17px medium and three lines at 15px in the soft ink, 24px padding) and a real fragment of the interface at true size (a control, a menu, a table slice, a swatch strip) docked flush against the opposite edge of the cell and cropped by it. The stagger is the idea: across the first row cells run text-top, fragment-top, text-top; the second row runs the reverse, so fragments form a checkerboard. Fragments differ in shape and size on purpose. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits left-aligned above the grid with 56px beneath it and no supporting line.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Statement cell, dark rows
entries.description: Two halves butted together, each 50vw wide and at least 90svh tall, with no gap. Left half, in a pale tone: the heading in three short lines at clamp(36px, 4.2vw, 68px), its middle line pushed flush right while the first and third stay flush left (text-align set per line), so the block zigzags inside the cell. A two-sentence paragraph of 30ch sits at the bottom-left and the single action at the bottom-right on the same baseline. Right half, in the darkest tone: four or five rows of equal height filling it, told apart by alternating two near-black tones, not by lines. Each row is a three-part grid: a title at 28px (5 parts), a short paragraph at 16px (4 parts) and a plain list of three terms at 15px (3 parts), all top-aligned with 28px padding. No images anywhere in the section.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Statements on colour fields
entries.description: Three or four full-bleed flat colour fields, each 72–80svh tall, butted together with no gap. Each field holds one benefit and is almost empty. The benefit is a phrase of two to four words at clamp(56px, 9vw, 150px), heavy, leading 0.9, on two lines at most, hugging the bottom-left corner with 28px margins. Its explanation is three lines at 17–18px, 30ch wide, placed near the top at column 8, so the eye travels the diagonal from small text to big phrase. On alternate fields the arrangement mirrors: phrase bottom-right and right-aligned, paragraph top-left at column 2. Text on each field is ink or paper, whichever contrasts more. There is no separate section heading: the first field's phrase is the heading. Nothing else appears on the fields: no images, shapes or buttons.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: The back of the card
entries.description: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Columns above, wordmark below
entries.description: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Contact as the headline
entries.description: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall. Top row, 40px from the edge: two or three short notes at 15px in columns 1–7 (address, hours, a one-line description) and a back-to-top text link at the right margin. Then a tall empty gap. In the lower half, the way to get in touch is the display line: the telephone number or the email address itself, set at 8–9vw, flush left, hard against the margin, as one link. An email address may break once, before the @, giving two lines. Size it with `clamp()` so the longest line fills at least 80% of the width. Under it, one row of small text at 14px spread across three positions: links at the left, credits in the centre, city and year at the right. The wordmark appears only small, in the top row.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Invitation over a cropped name
entries.description: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: The mark, built large
entries.description: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type. Across the full content width and about 34svh tall, the wordmark is built from blocks: each letter is knocked out of its own solid rectangle in a palette colour, the rectangles differ in height (60–100% of the band) and butt together with 4px gaps, bottoms on one line. Where the project has a simple geometric mark or motif, enlarge that instead, drawn as inline SVG from flat rectangles, circles and quarter-arcs with the same 4px gaps. Below, 56px lower: four columns of plain links at 15px across columns 1–8, and two addresses or contact lines in columns 9–12. A last row carries the copyright at the left and one small filled button at the right. Space and the block construction do all the separating.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Photograph half, menu half
entries.description: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: A footer of tiles
entries.description: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: A single quiet line
entries.description: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.

entries.title: Name first, places under it
entries.description: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Name across the last photograph
entries.description: The footer is the page's last photograph, full-bleed at 100vw by 100svh, darkened evenly with `filter: brightness(0.62)` so paper-coloured type reads everywhere on it. Three layers of text sit on the image. Top row, 32px from the edge: a short link list at 16px at the left margin and contact details at the right margin, each no wider than three columns. Mid-height is left to the photograph. Along the bottom, the wordmark runs the full width in the paper colour, letters about 12–20vw tall depending on the name's length, baseline 56px above the edge; under it one line of legal text at 13px. Choose an image whose interest is in its middle band, since the top and bottom carry text. No panel, no box and no colour block separates the footer from the image: the photograph is the footer.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Dense masonry sheet
entries.description: A three-line statement at 22px, 30ch wide, sits at the 66% column with 64px of space below it; it is the only large text. Then a dense masonry of about twenty tiles in six columns with 4px gaps and 12px outer margins, built with CSS `columns: 6; column-gap: 4px` and `break-inside: avoid` on each figure. Tile sizes range from 90px squares to one feature tile of 280 by 160px that sits above the first two columns, outside the column flow. Images keep their natural ratios, so column bottoms are ragged. Every tile has one caption line at 12px directly beneath, 6px below the image and 14px above the next tile, in the form name, comma, type. Mix photographs, posters, details and textures. No hover chrome; the sheet reads at a glance and fills the full width.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Drag row of mixed modules
entries.description: One horizontal row, 68svh tall, running off both viewport edges with 12px gaps, draggable and scrollable sideways (`overflow-x: auto`, `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`, scrollbar hidden). The row is built from three module types: a tall single image at 3:4 filling the row height; a column of two stacked 4:3 images sharing the height with a 12px gap; and a wide 16:10 landscape at full height. Sequence for nine photographs: tall, stacked pair, wide, stacked pair, tall, wide. The row starts 6vw in from the left, so the first module is whole and the last visible one is cut by the right edge. A heading of two or three words at 28–36px sits 32px above the row's left start; the count of photographs sits at the right margin on the same baseline. No captions and no arrows. Inside a narrow reading column the same row runs 300px tall and is cut by the column's edge.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Full-bleed sequence, text interlocked
entries.description: Three photographs, each 100vw by 100svh, shown one after another with nothing between them. Each is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside a wrapper 300svh tall, so the second slides up over the first and the third over the second like a curtain; no scroll hijacking. The section above interlocks with the first photograph: a narrow paragraph at 13–14px, 220px wide, sitting on the column line at 58% of the width, is pulled down with a negative bottom margin so its last four lines overlap the photograph's top edge, in a colour that reads on both ground and image. Each photograph carries one caption line at 15px in white at the bottom-left margin, over a neutral dark scrim limited to the lowest 120px. No heading. Choose three frames with the same light and a calm lower-left corner. The last photograph releases into the next section.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: One frame, contents change
entries.description: Instead of many pictures side by side, one frame stays in place and its contents change. The frame is small and exact: 300px square on a quiet page, or up to 40vw at 4:5 on an object-led one, centred or sitting on the text column's left edge, with at least 20vh of empty ground above and below. Five to seven photographs are stacked inside it with `position: absolute` and crossfade in turn (opacity over 600ms, each held for 2.4 seconds, via CSS keyframes with staggered delays). All are shot or cropped alike: same scale, same light direction, the subject at the same position, so only the subject seems to change. On a flat ground use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so studio backgrounds vanish. One caption line at 14px sits 16px below the frame and changes with the image. No arrows and no counter. On a motif-led page the frame takes the motif's shape through `clip-path`.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Photographs gathered round a heading
entries.description: A band about one screen tall on the plain page ground, used as the page's one deliberate rest. At its visual centre sits the heading, two lines at clamp(32px, 2.6vw, 40px) in a light weight, centred, with one sentence at 17px under it and a text link beneath that. Around it six to eight small photographs are scattered irregularly across the middle columns (x 320–1120; the outer 320px on each side stay empty, equally), each 160–200px wide at about 9:10, square corners, at different heights with 60–200px of air between them. Two of them come within 40px of the heading's block, which their drift never reaches, so the cluster reads as gathered round it rather than laid on a grid. No captions and no frames. Each photograph drifts at its own rate as the band passes (4–12% of its own height on a scroll-linked timeline), so the cluster loosens and tightens; under reduced motion it stays put. The pictures come from one place or one day and share one treatment.
entries.notes: Recipe metadata, not bundled font binaries or the referenced sites and photographs. Source-specific rights remain separate.

entries.title: Prints dropped on the headline
entries.description: A flat colour field 100svh tall. A two-line headline of two to four words in an ultra-condensed or ultra-heavy face is centred, each line clamp(120px, 14vw, 210px) tall with leading 0.85. Two portrait photographs, each about 26vw wide at 3:4 with an 8px solid white border like a print, are absolutely placed on top of the headline's centre: one rotated −8 degrees, one +6 degrees, overlapping each other by a third and hiding roughly half the letters, so the eye completes the words. A third, smaller print (16vw) may sit at the lower right, cropped by the section's bottom edge. One plain sentence at 16px sits at the bottom-left margin, 24px from the edges. The prints are above the type in the stacking order; hovering one brings it to the front and straightens it to 0 degrees over 200ms. Nothing else is on the field.

entries.title: Rising triptych
entries.description: A wrapper about 200svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh on the plain page ground. The heading, two lines at clamp(32px, 2.8vw, 44px), is centred in the top fifth of the stage with one sentence at 17px under it. From the bottom edge three photographs rise as the page scrolls, each at its own speed. The centre one, a 4:5 portrait, starts 620px wide with only its top quarter showing and grows (scale and travel on a scroll-linked timeline) until it is about 760px wide with its top 40px below the sentence, cropped by the bottom edge, so it never reaches the heading. In the study it slides over the heading; here nothing lies on top of a heading. The two outer ones, each 360×530px, stand beside it with 10px gaps, their tops always 55px lower than the centre's, and by the end they are cut by the left and right viewport edges. Square corners, no captions, one consistent light across all three (warm interiors with warm, cold coast with cold). Under reduced motion show the end state with the heading above the three photographs.

entries.title: Small frames, wide space
entries.description: A flat, quiet viewport 100svh tall in which about 70% of the screen is empty. At mid-height a single row of small portrait frames runs across and off both sides: each frame 11vw wide and 24svh tall (roughly 2:3), spaced 5vw apart, vertically centred, six or seven visible at 1440. Frames have square corners and sit directly on the ground with no border. The row scrolls sideways by drag or trackpad (`overflow-x: auto` with the scrollbar hidden) and may hold 12–24 frames. One line of text overlaps the top-left of the first frame by 12px: a title of two or three words at 20–24px followed by the count, placed above the frame in the stacking order. Hovering a frame scales it to 1.1 from its centre over 250ms; nothing else moves. No captions under frames, no arrows, and no other text in the section.
